title: Pool swapflow: minimal-tenant-surge rolling reconfig for dedicated GPU pools
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Performing fleet-wide node reconfigurations (kernel updates, CUDA/toolkit changes, hotpatches) currently causes large, simultaneous pod evictions in dedicated GPU pools which triggers autoscaler churn and customer-visible latency spikes. Existing approaches (fast drains or blanket evictions) either increase cost (overprovision) or break tenant SLAs.

Goal: Implement a "pool swapflow" pattern that lets us perform rolling reconfigurations with minimal concurrent tenant displacement and deterministic autoscaler handshakes. Swapflow must be compatible with dedicated pools, respect tenant slot reservations, and integrate with the autoscaler and rollout gate system so we can hit SLOs during maintenance windows.
acceptance_criteria: New swapflow controller can perform a full pool reconfiguration while ensuring at most 5% of tenant slots are force-evicted concurrently
Autoscaler handshake API is used to pause scaling-to-zero and honor maintenance padding during the operation
Canary tenant group (configurable) shows <10% tail-latency regression and <1% error-rate delta during a live 2-hour rehearsal
Operations console shows per-pool swapflow progress, tenant migration telemetry, and rollback buttons
End-to-end e2e test that simulates heavy tail workloads passes in CI (within 48h of PR merge)
technical_notes: Core idea: rather than draining whole nodes, we perform a "slot-preserving swap" where we provision temporary standby slots on a warmed pool and migrate tenants in micro-batches using an occupancy-aware token-bucket pace

Controller components: (1) Reservation API to record slot reservations and soft-fence tenant placement; (2) Migration scheduler that batches tenants by size/seq-len profile; (3) Autoscaler handshaker that requests temporary headroom and prevents scale-downs during final handoff; (4) Safety gate that monitors tail latency and aborts if SLOs are breached
Migration step uses KV-cache warmup hints: we prefetch likely KV prefixes for large sessions to reduce cold-KV misses post-move
We will add a temporary 'maintenance affinity' label so replicas are placed on standby nodes during the swap; affinity removed after validation
Edge case: preemptible tenant workloads may decline to relocate — treat them as non-migratable and leave pinned. Controller computes an adjusted headroom target to absorb pinned tenants
Compatibility: Controller will work with both Dedicated classic and Dedicated v2 pools; initial rollout targets Dedicated v2 only (safer API surface)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design): finalize Reservation API and autoscaler handshake spec — doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/Pool+Swapflow+Spec
Phase 1 (Prototype): implement controller, stub autoscaler handshake; internal test on dev cluster (eta 2 weeks) — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4182
Phase 2 (Integrate): wire autoscaler API, add maintenance-affinity label, add console controls for 'Start/Abort/Force-Complete'
Phase 3 (Canary): run swapflow on single low-tenancy pool during off-peak with canary tenant set; gate metrics: p99 latency, error-rate, eviction-count
Phase 4 (Broad rollout): enable opt-in for Dedicated customers; default off for public pools; guard with runtime-1.20 feature flag
Abort criteria: sustained p99 latency increase >20% for 15m OR error-rate increase >2% absolute for 5m
testing_plan: Unit tests for Reservation API and migration scheduler
Simulated cluster test that injects heterogeneous tenant sessions and validates concurrent-eviction cap
Load rehearsal against staging with live traffic replay for 2h across peak hours
Chaos scenario: simulate autoscaler failures and ensure controller performs safe pause + rollback
Post-mortem rehearsal: run full swapflow on canary pool and produce runbook updates
